page: RPC feature shares API specifications between server and client. Export typeof Hono app as AppType. hc() Hono Client accepts AppType generic to infer input/output types. Validation: Zod Validator (zValidator) or Standard Schema Validator. Client-side: import hc from hono/client, create client with hc<AppType>(url), call client.path.$method(). Response compatible with fetch Response. Cookies: add init { credentials: 'include' } option. Status codes explicitly specified in c.json() create typed responses. Global error responses via ApplyGlobalResponse type helper. Avoid c.notFound() for client type inference; use c.json() with status code instead. Path parameters passed as strings via param, query values with query. Single and multiple parameters supported. File uploads via form body with File object. Custom fetch method for Service Bindings. Query serialization via buildSearchParams option. URL generation: $url() returns URL object (requires absolute URL), $path() returns path string. Headers in requests via headers option. RequestInit via init option. Type inference: InferRequestType, InferResponseType, InferResponseType with status code. parseResponse() helper for type-safe response parsing. SWR integration example. RPC with larger apps: chain handlers, export AppType from chained routes. IDE performance issues with many routes; solutions: compile code beforehand, TypeScript project references, specify type manually, split app/client files. Known issues: version mismatch, handlers returning .then() chain lose types (use async/await). Questions: How do I set up RPC? How do I handle status codes? How do I use path parameters? sections.manifest: Server setup for RPC. Create route with validator using zValidator from 'hono/middleware/zod-validator'. Example: app.post('/posts', zValidator('form', z.object({...})), handler). Handler returns c.json({...}, statusCode). Export type AppType = typeof route. Alternative: Standard Schema Validator (Valibot, etc.). Configuration: tsconfig.json compilerOptions strict: true for monorepo. Questions: How do I set up server RPC? Which validators work? Why set strict mode?

Client setup for RPC. Import hc from 'hono/client', import type AppType from server. Create client: const client = hc<AppType>('http://localhost:8787/'). Call client.path.$method({data}). Response is fetch Response. Retrieve data with res.json(). Access status with res.ok, res.status. Cookies: add init: { credentials: 'include' } to hc options. Custom headers per request via headers option. Global headers via hc() option. Questions: How do I set up client RPC? What response methods are available? How do I send cookies?

Status code typing for responses. Specify status code in c.json(): c.json({ error: 'not found' }, 404). Client infers response by status code. InferResponseType<typeof client.path.$method> returns union of all response types. InferResponseType<typeof client.path.$method, 200> returns specific status type. Conditional type narrowing: if (res.status === 404) { ... }. Questions: How do I type different status codes? How do I infer response types by status?

ApplyGlobalResponse type helper for global error handlers. Merges app.onError() response types into all routes. Syntax: type AppWithErrors = ApplyGlobalResponse<typeof app, { 500: { json: { error: string } } }>. Multiple error codes: 401, 500, etc. Client knows about both success and error responses. InferResponseType includes global error types. Questions: How do I handle global errors? How do I type multiple error codes?

NotFound handling for RPC. Avoid c.notFound() as client cannot infer type (data is unknown). Use c.json() with status code instead: c.json({ error: 'not found' }, 404). Alternative: module augmentation to extend NotFoundResponse interface with TypedResponse. Syntax: declare module 'hono' { interface NotFoundResponse extends Response, TypedResponse<{...}, 404, 'json'> }. Benefits: enables c.notFound() with type inference. Questions: Why avoid c.notFound()? How do I type notFound responses?

Path parameters and query values handling. Parameters must be passed as strings even if coerced to other types. Syntax: client.path[':id'].$get({ param: { id: '123' }, query: { page: '1' } }). Validator converts: z.coerce.number() converts string '1' to 1. Multiple parameters: client.path[':postId'][':authorId'].$get({...}). Slashes in parameters: use regexp /posts/:id{.+} on server, encodeURIComponent on client recommended. Questions: How do I pass path parameters? How do I handle query values? How do I include slashes in parameters?

Custom headers for requests. Per-request headers via headers option: client.path.$get({...}, { headers: { 'X-Custom': 'value' } }). Global headers via hc() option: hc<AppType>(url, { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer TOKEN' } }). Questions: How do I add custom headers? How do I set global headers?

RequestInit option for fetch RequestInit. Pass via init option: client.path.$post({...}, { init: { signal: abortController.signal } }). AbortController for request cancellation. init takes highest priority, can override body, method, headers. Questions: How do I abort requests? How do I pass RequestInit?

$url() returns URL object for endpoint. Requires absolute URL (not relative /). Syntax: client.api.posts.$url() returns URL. Path parameter: client.api.posts[':id'].$url({ param: { id: '123' } }). Typed URL via second type parameter: hc<AppType, 'http://localhost:8787'>(). Useful for type-safe keys in SWR. Caveat: relative URLs throw 'Invalid URL' error. Questions: How do I get URL from endpoint? When do I use $url()? How do I type URL precisely?

$path() returns path string without base URL origin. Works with relative or absolute base URLs. Syntax: client.api.posts.$path() returns '/api/posts'. Path parameters: client.api.posts[':id'].$path({ param: { id: '123' } }). Query parameters: client.api.posts.$path({ query: { page: '1', limit: '10' } }) returns '/api/posts?page=1&limit=10'. Questions: How do I get path string? When do I use $path()? How do I add query to path?

File uploads via form body. Client: client.path.$put({ form: { file: new File([...], filename, { type: '...' }) } }). Server validation: z.object({ file: z.instanceof(File) }). Questions: How do I upload files? How do I validate file uploads?

Custom fetch method for Service Bindings. Useful for Cloudflare Workers Service Bindings. Syntax: hc<AppType>(url, { fetch: c.env.SERVICE.fetch.bind(c.env.SERVICE) }). Example wrangler.toml: services = [{ binding = 'AUTH', service = 'auth-service' }]. Questions: How do I use Service Bindings? How do I set custom fetch?

Custom query serializer via buildSearchParams option. Customize URLSearchParams creation. Example: bracket notation for arrays: 'key[]'. Skip undefined values. Function: buildSearchParams(query) returns URLSearchParams. Questions: How do I customize query serialization? When do I use bracket notation?

Type inference utilities. InferRequestType<typeof client.path.$method> gets request type. InferRequestType<typeof $post>['form'] gets form data type. InferResponseType<typeof $post> gets response type. Usage: narrow down specific input/output shapes. Questions: How do I infer request types? How do I infer response types?

parseResponse() helper for type-safe response parsing. Import from 'hono/client'. Automatically parses based on Content-Type. Throws error if response not ok. Usage: const result = await parseResponse(client.hello.$get()).catch(e => {...}). DetailedError type for error handling. Questions: How do I parse responses safely? What does parseResponse do?

SWR integration with Hono RPC. Import useSWR from 'swr'. Create client with hc<AppType>. Define fetcher using InferRequestType. useSWR(key, fetcher(arg)). Returns { data, error, isLoading }. Syntax pattern in React component. Questions: How do I use SWR with Hono? How do I type SWR fetcher?

RPC with larger modular applications. Chain handlers for type inference: .get(...).post(...).get(...). Export AppType = typeof chainedRoutes. Sub-apps: authors.ts, books.ts with separate Hono instances, main index.ts chains via .route('/authors', authors).route('/books', books). Export AppType from combined result. Client creation same as normal. Questions: How do I use RPC with modular apps? How do I chain multiple apps?

Known issues and performance solutions. IDE slowness with many routes: massive type instantiations. Hono version mismatch between backend/frontend causes '_Type instantiation is excessively deep' error. Solutions: (1) Use TypeScript project references for monorepo. (2) Compile code beforehand: use hcWithType trick to calculate types at compile-time. (3) Specify type arguments manually: new Hono().get<'path'>('path', ...). (4) Split app/client into multiple files. (5) Handlers returning .then() chain lose types; use async/await instead. (6) Annotate TypedResponse on .then() if necessary. Tools: turborepo, concurrently, npm-run-all for build coordination. Questions: Why is IDE slow? How do I fix version mismatch? How do I improve performance? What's wrong with .then() chains?
